## Outcome

I merged a Chromote timeout fix and opened focused investigations covering GitHub Pages permissions, multiline facet strips, and the `atime` workflow.

## What I Did

- Opened Issue #334 and [PR #337](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/337) after finding that an early renderer test set a shared Chromote session’s `default_timeout` to one second.
- Removed the unsafe setting and restored a safe page timeout. PR #337 merged June 12.
- Opened Issue #335 and [PR #338](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/338) to investigate GitHub Pages tests when forked PRs lack the organization token.
- Opened [PR #339](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/339), first adding a failing multiline facet-strip test, then joining labels with newlines and rendering lines as SVG `<tspan>` elements.
- Opened Issue #340 and [PR #341](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/341) after tracing an `atime` failure to the workflow pre-installing current Animint2 before building an older baseline commit.

## Learnings

“Flaky” often describes appearance rather than cause. Shared browser state, shared external repositories, missing credentials, and the wrong package in a library can each produce intermittent-looking failures with deterministic roots.

## Challenges / Notes

Not every diagnosis belongs in Animint2 or in `testthat`. Workflow failures may require a workflow-level guard, an upstream fix, or a documented closure instead of more package code.

## Next Week Targets

Decide which proposals belong in Animint2, which should be simplified, and which should move to another maintenance boundary.
